Hi Marcus. Your home improvement loan application **LN-4471 was declined on January 14, 2027**. The automated underwriting score was **611**, below the approval cutoff of **640**.

You should receive an **adverse action notice** explaining the principal reasons for the decision and how to request additional information. If a consumer credit report influenced the decision, the notice will also identify the credit bureau and explain your right to obtain a free copy of that report and dispute inaccurate information.

Review the notice carefully before reapplying. If you believe information was incorrect or would like to ask about reconsideration, contact the lender using the details provided in that notice.

Hi Marcus. Your **home improvement loan application (LN-4471) currently shows “Declined.”** The automated model recorded a score of **611**, below the **640** approval cutoff.

However, the file lists the decision date as **January 14, 2027**, which is in the future relative to today, **July 29, 2026**. That appears to be a record error, so I can’t confirm when the decision was formally issued.

### What happens next
- You should receive a written adverse-action notice stating the specific principal reasons for the denial—or explaining how to request them within 60 days. A score below the cutoff alone is not considered a sufficiently specific reason. ([consumerfinance.gov](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1002/2023-04-19/9/?utm_source=openai))
- If a consumer credit report influenced the decision, the notice should identify the reporting agency, provide applicable credit-score information, and explain your right to request a free report within 60 days and dispute errors. ([consumerfinance.gov](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/my-credit-application-was-denied-because-of-my-credit-report-what-can-i-do-en-1253/?utm_source=openai))
- Because your application is marked complete, federal rules generally require notification within 30 days after the completed application is received. ([consumerfinance.gov](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1002/2023-04-19/9/?utm_source=openai))

Please contact application support and reference **LN-4471** to verify the decision date and delivery of your notice.

Hi Marcus — your **home improvement loan application (LN-4471) was declined on January 14, 2027**. Your file shows the automated underwriting score was **611**, below the **640** approval cutoff.

What to expect next:

- Under [Regulation B § 1002.9](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1002/9/), you should receive an adverse-action notice within 30 days of the completed application. It must provide the principal reasons for the denial or explain how to request them within 60 days.
- Because an automated model made the decision, Colorado’s [Artificial Intelligence Act](https://leg.colorado.gov/bills/sb24-205) requires additional information about the model’s role and the data used. The notice must also explain your rights to request access or corrections to that data and to seek meaningful human review and reconsideration where technically and commercially reasonable.
- If a consumer credit report or credit score was used, the notice must include further disclosures, including how to obtain a free report and dispute inaccuracies, under [FCRA § 615](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/using-consumer-reports-credit-decisions-what-know-about-adverse-action-risk-based-pricing-notices).

Hi Dolores. Your home improvement loan application **LN-5182 was declined on January 14, 2027**. The automated underwriting score was **611**, below the approval cutoff of **640**.

What to expect next:

- You’ll receive an adverse-action notice stating the specific principal reason(s) for the decision, generally within 30 days of the completed application. See [Regulation B § 1002.9 — Adverse action notification](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1002/9/).
- Because the loan would be secured by your California owner-occupied residence, you’ll also receive California’s Fair Lending Notice and applicable complaint-contact information. See [California Housing Financial Discrimination Act — Fair Lending Notice and statement of reasons](https://dfpi.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/337/2021/10/DFPI-1977-FAIR-LENDING-NOTICE.pdf).
- If a consumer credit report or credit score contributed to the decision, the notice will identify the reporting agency and explain your rights to obtain a free report within 60 days and dispute inaccuracies. See [FCRA § 615 — Adverse action notice](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/using-consumer-reports-credit-decisions-what-know-about-adverse-action-risk-based-pricing-notices).
